note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart deliberately. Claims about the world (how many courts a venue has, what a session costs, whether it is lit) come from the City of Tallahassee and are cited. Claims about coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Leon County, and are worded so a reader cannot mistake one for the other.

slots.coverage:
One city in Leon County is published here: Tallahassee, with seven venues and thirty-four courts checked against the City's own pickleball page. Thirty-three of them are outdoors and one is inside Jake Gaither Community Center.

Nothing else in the county has been read. Leon County's own parks have not been checked against a named source, so none appears anywhere on this site and this page does not characterise them.

What the City of Tallahassee writes down is a count and an address for every venue, a weekly grid of Open Play, Reserved Play and first-come hours for the outdoor courts, a price table for Reserved Play, a free answer for Open Play, hours at one venue, lighting at one, and surface nowhere.

Five Tallahassee venues are named on the city page but not published here. Four Oaks Park has six courts "used for pickleball only" and a schedule seven days a week, at an address neither address resolver can find. Four community centres, Lawrence-Gregory, Lincoln, Sue Herndon McCollum and the Tallahassee Senior Center, are on the City's indoor schedule with sessions and no court count, and Lincoln reads "renovations in progress" on every day.
slots.distribution:
What we cover sits in one city and, within it, splits between parks and community centres in a way the City's own list makes plain. Three of the seven venues are parks: Tom Brown with twelve courts, Winthrop with six, Lafayette with two. Four are community centres with courts outside the building: LeVerne Payne with six, Walker-Ford with three, Jake Gaither with two outdoors and one in, McLean with two.

Eighteen of the thirty-four courts are at the two parks the City takes online reservations for, Tom Brown and Winthrop. Fourteen of those eighteen are tennis courts doing double duty, eight of Tom Brown's on "tennis courts 1-4" and all six of Winthrop's "multi-purpose courts".

The useful pattern is the schedule rather than the map. Two venues carry free Open Play sessions, LeVerne Payne and Tom Brown, and they are the two where a rotation is guaranteed by the City's timetable. Two carry paid Reserved Play, Tom Brown and Winthrop. Four are first come, first play at every hour with no session at all. Lighting is stated once, at Walker-Ford. Hours are stated once, at Jake Gaither. The one indoor court in the published set is Jake Gaither's, on a Friday lunchtime, Reserved Play only.
slots.gaps:
This is a Tallahassee page under a county heading, and the gap will not close by accident. Leon County's own parks have not been read, no other operator in the county has been read, and nothing here says whether anything outside the City would clear the threshold of three venues with a named source and a date.

Inside Tallahassee the gaps are of two kinds. The first is the five refused venues, which are real places on the City's own list. Four Oaks is the expensive one: six dedicated courts, Open Play and Reserved Play seven days a week to 10:00pm, online booking, and an address, "5151 Four Oaks Boulevard", that returns nothing from the Census address file and nothing at house-number level from OpenStreetMap. The four indoor centres fail on a number the City has not written.

The second kind is silence inside the published venues. There is no surface anywhere, lighting at one venue in seven, hours at one, and a resurfacing notice at McLean dated December 2025 that was still on the page in September 2026.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Leon County?
faqs.a: Nobody publishes an answer for the whole county. What has been checked is 34 courts across seven venues, all in Tallahassee, each with a source and a date you can see. The City of Tallahassee alone names five further venues that cannot be published here, one of them with six pickleball-only courts, and no other operator in the county has been read.

faqs.q: Are the courts on this page free?
faqs.a: Two venues are, during Open Play: LeVerne Payne and Tom Brown, where the City writes that "all Open Play sessions are drop-in and free". Reserved Play at Tom Brown and Winthrop costs $3.50 to $5.75 a session. The other four venues are first come, first play with no stated price, so they carry no fee answer.

One. At Walker-Ford Community Center the City writes that night play is available at its three courts. No other venue in the county's published set carries a lighting statement, so the rest are recorded as not stated rather than lit or unlit.

sources.evidence: The City's pickleball page, which lists each outdoor venue with an address, a count line and a weekly grid: Four Oaks Park "5151 Four Oaks Boulevard", "6 courts", "used for pickleball only", Open Play and Reserved Play daily to 10:00pm; LeVerne Payne Community Center "2 courts with adjustable net straps, 4 courts with portable nets if needed and all have painted lines", Open Play Tue/Thu/Sat; Tom Brown Park "4 pickleball courts | 8 pickleball courts on multi-purpose courts (tennis courts 1-4)", Open Play Mon/Wed/Sun, Reserved Play Mon-Thu evenings and Tue/Thu/Sat mornings; Winthrop Park "6 courts", "multi-purpose courts used for tennis, pickleball and any other sports", Reserved Play Mon-Thu evenings and Sat morning; Jack L. McLean Jr. Community Center "2 courts with adjustable net straps and painted lines", FCFP Only, "unavailable for  use until december 5, 2025"; Jake Gaither Community Center "1 indoor court, 2 outdoor courts", "Outdoor FCFP: 8:00am - 9:00pm Daily, Closed on Sunday", indoor Fri 12:00pm-2:00pm "Rerseve Play Only"; Lafayette Park "2 courts with net tie-downs", FCFP Only; Walker-Ford Community Center "3 courts - night play is available", FCFP Only. Indoor entries with sessions and no count: Lawrence-Gregory, Lincoln ("No Pickleball (renovations in progress)"), Sue Herndon McCollum, Tallahassee Senior Center ("$3 Donation Encouraged"). "Court reservations can only be made for Reserved Play sessions, as all Open Play sessions are drop-in and free." "Singles - $5.75 Singles Senior* - $4.75 Doubles - $4.25 Doubles Senior* - $3.50". Online reservations for Four Oaks, Tom Brown and Winthrop, or 850-891-4940. Snapshot: data/sources/tallahassee/pickleball.html
sources.not_stated: Anything about Leon County's own parks or any operator other than the City of Tallahassee; surface at any venue; lighting other than Walker-Ford's phrase; hours other than Jake Gaither's.

sources.evidence: The seven published addresses matched at house-number level and were placed in Leon County, FL (FIPS 12073), inside the incorporated place Tallahassee city - five through the Census address file as the City writes them, and two (Tom Brown Park as "501 EASTERWOOD DR", Lafayette Park as "501 INGLESIDE AVE") on Census answers that change the City's street type where OpenStreetMap holds nothing for the City's spelling. "5151 Four Oaks Boulevard", the address the City publishes for Four Oaks Park, is found by neither resolver. Snapshot: data/sources/tallahassee-county-census.json
